summary: Produce a read-only project description for SSHPeaches by inspecting repository structure, README/docs, source layout, tests, and git status. The description should distinguish documented capabilities from source-confirmed implementation and inferred architecture, and should include a concise caveat about any current uncommitted work without treating it as complete or stable.
assumptions: The request is informational: describe the project in the final response, not create or modify repository files.
The execution policy for this run is read-only; no existing files or directories should be modified, deleted, renamed, moved, or type-changed.
Existing modified and untracked files belong to prior work and should only be observed, not changed.
A balanced technical onboarding description is acceptable without asking the user to choose a specific audience first.

tasks.title: Inventory repository structure
tasks.description: Read top-level files and directory layout to identify the Gradle project, Android app module, source sets, documentation folders, test folders, and configuration files.
verification: Root Gradle files and app module layout are identified.
Documentation, Android source, unit tests, and instrumentation tests are separately described.
Tooling/context directories such as .codex, .agents, or .stringbean are not treated as product source unless directly relevant.

tasks.title: Summarize documented purpose and capabilities
tasks.description: Use README and docs content to describe the project's stated purpose and user-facing capabilities, carefully labeling these as documented features unless implementation is also verified in source.
verification: Summary matches README and documentation claims.
Documented goals are not overstated as fully implemented behavior unless source inspection supports that claim.

tasks.title: Summarize technical architecture
tasks.description: Inspect source package names and major app files to describe the Android architecture, likely UI/state layers, SSH/session components, settings/persistence areas, input handling, and test utilities. Clearly mark inferred architecture where source names imply behavior but detailed implementation is not fully reviewed.
verification: Architecture summary references real repository paths or source areas.
Confirmed implementation facts are distinguished from reasonable inferences.
The summary stays concise and contributor-oriented.

tasks.title: Summarize current worktree state
tasks.description: Use read-only git status inspection to identify broad active change areas, if any. Present them as current worktree context only, without claiming the changes are complete, tested, or intended for release.
verification: Major modified and untracked areas from git status are represented at a high level.
No dirty worktree file is modified or reverted.
The description clearly separates committed project structure from current local changes.

tasks.title: Prepare concise project description
tasks.description: Produce a human-readable project description suitable for onboarding, with sections covering purpose, main capabilities, repository layout, architecture overview, tests/docs, license or project metadata if present, and current worktree caveat.
verification: Description is clear for a new contributor.
Description is concise enough to be useful in a README, handoff note, or project summary.
Facts are traceable to repository files or explicitly framed as inferences.
No file creation, edit, build, test, or other write-producing operation is performed.

risks: README or docs may describe intended capabilities that are only partially implemented in the current source.
The worktree may be dirty, so observed local state may differ from the last committed project state.
Some architecture details may require inference from filenames and package layout if a full source audit is too broad for a concise project description.
Read-only policy prevents creating a documentation artifact or running build/test commands that would generate outputs.
